rules.name: Methodology Requirement
rules.desc:
Methodology courses should be selected based on their potential to support the student's projected capstone project.
Methodology courses must be taken for 3-5 units and a letter grade.
rules.notes: Note that Methodology courses may not be offered every year. For an up-to-date list of this academic year's Methodology courses, visit the Core Coursework page on the CCSRE website.

rules.name: Community-Engaged Learning Requirement
rules.desc: CCSRE students must complete at least one Community-Engaged Learning (CEL) course or co-curricular experience that centers issues of race, ethnicity, and inequality. This requirement may be fulfilled by enrolling in a Cardinal Course, complete a CCSRE Undergraduate Fellowship, or participating in an Alternative Spring Break. The CEL requirement may be fulfilled by courses that also fulfill other CSRE degree requirements (e.g., a Methodology course may also count toward the CEL requirement). The CEL requirement may be fulfilled by academic experiences, such as fellowships, that do not carry academic units.
rules.notes: See the Community-Engaged Learning course list on the Core Coursework page on the CCSRE website for this year's curricular offerings.

rules.name: CSRE Electives (remaining units of the 60)

limits.label: DAAAS, ASNAMST, CHILATST, JEWISHST and NATIVEAM courses

rules.desc:
CSRE majors must complete the remaining units of their 60-unit minimum with elective coursework in the CCSRE family of programs, with the exception below.
CSRE majors may count up to 15 units of Department of African and African American Studies (DAAAS), Asian American Studies (ASNAMST), Chicana/o-Latina/o Studies (CHILATST), Jewish Studies (JEWISHST), or Native American Studies (NATIVEAM) courses toward their elective coursework in the CSRE major (including subplan units).

rules.name: Writing in the Major (WIM)
rules.notes:
CCSRE students must plan to complete 200X or 201X in person on Stanford campus in autumn of their final year of study.
Note that the same five-unit course fulfills the WIM and Capstone requirements.

rules.name: Honors (optional)

children.name: Honors proposal approved by a CCSRE faculty advisor (spring before the final year)
GPA of at least 3.7 in the major and 3.5 overall, kept until graduation
B+ or above on the honors thesis

rules.desc:
Honors students must apply with a complete proposal approved by a CCSRE faculty advisor in the spring preceding their final year of study. Honors students must continuously enroll at Stanford in autumn, winter, and spring. For more information about the Honors program and the application process, visit the Honors page on the CCSRE website.
Honors applications are open to students with a grade point average (GPA) of at least 3.7 in the major and 3.5 overall. Students must receive a B+ or above on their thesis and maintain the GPA minimum until graduation in order to receive Honors.
rules.notes: A minimum grade of C- is required for a student to count a class towards the Core Curriculum, including the WIM and Capstone requirements.

rules.name: Overview
rules.desc: The subplan in Education and Inequality explores history, policy, and practice in education to understand how educational opportunity and learning outcomes are shaped by race, ethnicity, and power. Students develop an understanding of the core issues facing educators and policymakers and prepare to contribute to social and political discourse about education and opportunity.
rules.notes: Students must complete a minimum of 15 units of subplan-focused courses as part of the 60 units taken toward the major. All courses taken toward the subplan must be listed or cross-listed in the CCSRE family of programs; exceptions must be petitioned.

rules.name: 15 units of Education and Inequality subplan courses (CCSRE family)
Overview
rules.desc: The Environmental Justice subplan develops students’ understanding of the uneven and far-reaching impacts of environmental policy, climate change, grassroots environmental movements, and more. Students develop facility with various methodologies and leave prepared to work toward just environments for all.
rules.notes: Students must complete a minimum of 15 units of subplan-focused courses as part of the 60 units taken toward the major. All courses taken toward the subplan must be listed or cross-listed in the CCSRE family of programs; exceptions must be petitioned.

rules.name: 15 units of Environmental Justice subplan courses (CCSRE family)
Overview
rules.desc: The subplan in Health and Wellness supports interdisciplinary exploration of health research, access, and policy. Students take qualitative and quantitative approaches to understanding how health and wellness are defined and impacted by processes of racialization.
rules.notes: Students must complete a minimum of 15 units of subplan-focused courses as part of the 60 units taken toward the major. All courses taken toward the subplan must be listed or cross-listed in the CCSRE family of programs; exceptions must be petitioned.

rules.name: 15 units of Health and Wellness subplan courses (CCSRE family)
Overview
rules.desc: The Diversity and Aesthetics subplan explores the intersections of culture, race, and social transformation. Students experiment with how the arts, activism, and academic research come together to enact aesthetic and societal change.
rules.notes: Students must complete a minimum of 15 units of subplan-focused courses as part of the 60 units taken toward the major. All courses taken toward the subplan must be listed or cross-listed in the CCSRE family of programs; exceptions must be petitioned.

rules.name: 15 units of Identity, Diversity, and Aesthetics subplan courses (CCSRE family)
Overview
rules.desc: The Politics, Policy, and Equity subplan focuses on how political institutions, public policy, nonprofits, and social movements shape and are shaped by race and ethnicity. This subplan gives students the tools and frameworks to examine the ramifications of politics and policy on processes of racializaiton.
rules.notes: Students must complete a minimum of 15 units of subplan-focused courses as part of the 60 units taken toward the major. All courses taken toward the subplan must be listed or cross-listed in the CCSRE family of programs; exceptions must be petitioned.

rules.name: 15 units of Politics, Policy, and Equity subplan courses (CCSRE family)
Overview
rules.desc: Drawing from the contributions of feminism and queer of color studies, this concentration challenges normative constructions of race and ethnicity by equipping students with analytical tools from feminist theory, queer theory, post-colonial theory, critical race theory, and other critical methods.
rules.notes: Students must complete a minimum of 15 units of subplan-focused courses as part of the 60 units taken toward the major. All courses taken toward the subplan must be listed or cross-listed in the CCSRE family of programs; exceptions must be petitioned.

rules.name: 15 units of Race, Gender, and Sexuality subplan courses (CCSRE family)
Overview
rules.desc: The Race, Space, and Belonging subplan examines issues of immigration, citizenship, empire, gentrification, segregation, urban and rural space, human rights, public welfare, social justice, and law. Students examine how race and ethnicity shape constructions of and access to space, nation, and public resources.
rules.notes: Students must complete a minimum of 15 units of subplan-focused courses as part of the 60 units taken toward the major. All courses taken toward the subplan must be listed or cross-listed in the CCSRE family of programs; exceptions must be petitioned.

rules.name: 15 units of Race, Space, and Belonging subplan courses (CCSRE family)
Overview
rules.desc: Students in the subplan explore the relationship between technology, media, and racialization. Race and ethnicity are crucial for understanding the meaning, power, and evolution of technologies–from type, photography, film, and radio to social media, artificial intelligence, and algorithms. Students assess technological equity and reimagine how technology might be harnessed to actualize a more just and equitable world.
rules.notes: Students must complete a minimum of 15 units of subplan-focused courses as part of the 60 units taken toward the major. All courses taken toward the subplan must be listed or cross-listed in the CCSRE family of programs; exceptions must be petitioned.

rules.name: 15 units of Technology and Media subplan courses (CCSRE family)
Overview
rules.desc: A proposal for a self-designed subplan should include a description of the student’s focus, an articulation of why current subplans cannot accommodate it, a course plan, and a description of how each course meets the student’s educational objectives. Proposals for a self-designed subplan must be submitted with a student’s Major Declaration Proposal and will be reviewed by the CCSRE Academic Programs team.
rules.notes: Students must complete a minimum of 15 units of subplan-focused courses as part of the 60 units taken toward the major. All courses taken toward the subplan must be listed or cross-listed in the CCSRE family of programs; exceptions must be petitioned.

rules.name: 15 units of Self-Designed subplan courses (CCSRE family)
Self-designed subplan proposal approved by the CCSRE Academic Programs team

grading: All courses must be taken for a letter grade, unless only offered S/NC. A minimum grade of C- is required for a student to count a class towards the Core Curriculum, including the Gateway, Comparative Core, Methodology, WIM, and Capstone requirements. Additional units toward the major require a passing grade of D- or above. Student may count 2 classes with Satisfactory/No Credit (SNC) grading basis toward Additional Units.
policies:
Language courses do not count toward CSRE major requirements.
Course Petition Policy: No more than 15 units of petitioned courses that are not listed under CCSRE or cross-listed with CCSRE may be applied to the CSRE major. Students who wish to petition a course must fill out and submit a course petition form for the CCSRE Academic Programs team to review within one month of completing their annual degree audit meeting with the CCSRE Student Services Officer.
transferPolicy: Up to 20 units of external credit may be applied toward elective coursework in the major.
reviewNotes: The audit checks the 60 units of the major: CSRE 100, two of the three Comparative Core courses, one Methodology course of 3 or more units, the Community-Engaged Learning course (which can be a course that also counts elsewhere), CSRE 200X or 201X for the WIM and capstone, 15 units in your subplan and electives from the CCSRE family of programs. At most 15 of your elective and subplan units can come from AFRICAAM, ASNAMST, CHILATST, JEWISHST and NATIVEAM courses (a CSRE course cross-listed there counts too). The core, Methodology, WIM and capstone courses need a letter grade and a C- or better; electives and subplan courses need a letter grade (D- or better) unless the course is only offered S/NC. You check by hand that no more than two elective or subplan classes are S/NC, that subplan courses fit the subplan's focus, petitioned courses from outside CCSRE (at most 15 units), a CEL fellowship or Alternative Spring Break, and for honors the proposal, the 3.7 major and 3.5 overall GPA and the B+ thesis grade.
